name: Mumble
tagline: Open source VoIP for gamers. Low latency, self-hosted, secure.
shortDescription: Mumble is the gold-standard open source VoIP for low-latency voice chat. Used by gaming communities, esports, and distributed teams. Self-hosted server, cross-platform client.
longDescription:
## What it is

Mumble is an open source VoIP client/server. The client is called Mumble, the server is called Murmur. Low-latency, high-quality voice, positional audio (for games), strong encryption, cross-platform clients.

## Why we recommend it

If you need low-latency voice chat (lower than Discord, lower than Teams), Mumble is the answer. The protocol is designed for gaming — positional audio, push-to-talk, very low CPU.

## When to use it

- Gaming communities that want low-latency voice
- Esports teams (Mumble is the de facto standard)
- Distributed teams that prioritize voice quality over video
- Replacing TeamSpeak or Ventrilo
installInstructions:
**Server (Ubuntu):**
```
apt install mumble-server
dpkg-reconfigure mumble-server
```

**Client:** Download from mumble.info (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android).
pricingDetails: Free. BSD-licensed. Self-host on any server.
